name: Chennai–Kanyakumari Highway
aka: East Coast Road (ECR) — the coastal stretch south of Puducherry
Chennai–Tindivanam stretch follows the GST Road (old NH 45)
Includes most of the former NH 45A (Puducherry–Nagapattinam)

timeline.event: Coastal highway extended south to Thoothukudi
Extended further to end near Kanyakumari, meeting NH 44

history: NH 32 runs from Chennai to India's southern tip near Kanyakumari. It leaves Chennai on the busy GST Road through Tambaram, Chengalpattu and Tindivanam, reaches the sea at the former French town of Puducherry, and then follows the coast through fishing harbours and temple towns for the rest of the way. It became one long national highway in stages, reaching Thoothukudi in 2017 and Kanyakumari in 2022.
facts: South of Puducherry it forms the longest part of the East Coast Road, staying close to the Bay of Bengal.
The famous beach drive from Chennai past Mamallapuram to Puducherry is a separate coastal road — NH 32 itself runs a little inland on that stretch.
Connects the basilica town of Velankanni and the seaside temple town of Tiruchendur.
Ends near Anjugramam, where it meets NH 44, the Srinagar–Kanyakumari highway.
